docs.text: Driver CANOPEN_CLIENT Driver ¶ A generic C++20 CANopen client over a classic CAN frame port: NMT master, SDO client, heartbeat, emergency, SYNC, PDOs and a CiA 402 drive state machine. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver is not tied to a product or to a CAN controller. You give it a small class that sends one 11-bit frame, waits for one and reads a microsecond clock; it does the rest: the SDO transfer rules, heartbeat ageing, the emergency queue, PDO configuration in the order the profile prescribes and the drive's state transitions. Read and write objects (SDO) ¶ canopen_client :: Error ConfigureNode ( Client & client ) { // Expedited for 1 to 4 bytes, segmented for more; the driver picks. if ( auto r = client . SdoWriteU16 ( 5 , 0x2001 , 0 , 1234 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // SdoAbort: the node refused, `client.GetLastAbort()` says why } const auto value = client . SdoReadU32 ( 5 , 0x2000 , 0 ); if ( ! value ) { return value . error ; } std :: array < uint8_t , 64 > name {}; const auto n = client . SdoUpload ( 5 , 0x1008 , 0 , name ); // device name: a segmented read return n . error ; // BufferTooSmall if the node has more than 64 bytes } Sizes of 1 to 4 bytes travel as one expedited exchange, larger ones as a segmented transfer; the driver picks. After SdoAbort , GetLastAbort() holds the node, object and the 32-bit abort code, and canopen_client::AbortCodeName() names the common ones. For diagnosis there is a raw, single-shot path: ReadRawSdo() and WriteRawSdo() send one request and return the node's reply frame as it is; SendRawFrame() and ReadRawFrame() put one frame on the bus or take one from it; GetLastRawFrame() holds the last frame the driver saw. None of them retries or checks more than the framing. They bypass the safety and state guards and do not update the node table, so use SendNmt() , DriveDisable() and DriveQuickStop() to stop a node. A boot-up message leaves bootup_seen set for its node until ClearBootUp(node) . Watch nodes and read emergencies ¶ canopen_client :: Error WatchNode ( Client & client ) { if ( auto r = client . MonitorNode ( 5 , 3'000'000 ); ! r ) { // alive while a heartbeat is under 3 s old return r . error ; } const auto frame = client . Poll ( 100'000 ); // wait up to 100 ms and route one frame if ( ! frame ) { return frame . error ; } const auto status = client . GetNodeStatus ( 5 ); if ( status && ! status . value . alive ) { return canopen_client :: Error :: Timeout ; // no heartbeat for 3 s } canopen_client :: EmcyEvent event {}; while ( client . PopEmcy ( event )) { // event.node, event.code (0x0000 means the error is gone), event.error_register } return canopen_client :: Error :: Ok ; } Poll() is the receive loop: call it from your task with the longest wait you can afford. It routes one frame to the node table, the EMCY queue, a TPDO sample or the SYNC counter and returns which. Heartbeats are consumed only for nodes registered with MonitorNode() ; GuardNode() is the polled alternative for nodes that answer node guarding. Process data ¶ canopen_client :: Error SetUpPositionPdo ( Client & client ) { canopen_client :: PdoConfig pdo {}; pdo . cob_id = 0x185 ; // TPDO1 of node 5 pdo . transmission_type = 1 ; // sent on every SYNC pdo . entry_count = 2 ; pdo . entries [ 0 ] = { 0x6064 , 0 , 32 }; // position actual value pdo . entries [ 1 ] = { 0x6041 , 0 , 16 }; // statusword if ( auto r = client . ConfigurePdo ( 5 , canopen_client :: PdoKind :: Transmit , 1 , pdo ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // the PDO is left invalid, never half configured and valid } if ( auto r = client . SubscribeTpdo ( 0x185 , 6 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = client . SendNmt ( canopen_client :: NmtCommand :: Start , 5 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } return client . SendSync (). error ; // the node answers with the PDO; `Poll()` then `ReadTpdo(0x185)` } ConfigurePdo() writes the node's communication and mapping records in the profile's order, so the PDO is never valid while half written. Configure a node in Pre-operational and start it with SendNmt(Start, node) ; a node sends its TPDOs only when Operational. Drive a CiA 402 node ¶ canopen_client :: Error RunDrive ( Client & client ) { using canopen_client :: OperationMode ; if ( auto r = client . SetDriveMode ( 5 , OperationMode :: ProfileVelocity ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = client . DriveEnable ( 5 ); ! r ) { // shutdown, switch on, enable operation return r . error ; // DriveFault: the drive is in Fault; `DriveResetFault()` clears it } // ... write the target velocity (object 0x60FF) with `SdoWriteU32()` ... return client . DriveDisable ( 5 ). error ; // never refused, sent up to Config::safety_attempts times } DriveEnable() walks the state machine one transition at a time, writing the next controlword and reading the statusword until the drive reports Operation enabled or Config::drive_timeout_us of bus time passes, however small the poll period. A drive that maps its objects elsewhere passes a DriveObjects with its indices. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( canopen_client :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case canopen_client :: Error :: Timeout : return "no reply in time: node absent, wrong node id or bit rate" ; case canopen_client :: Error :: SdoAbort : return "the node refused the transfer: see GetLastAbort()" ; case canopen_client :: Error :: NodeState : return "the node is Stopped: send NmtCommand::Start or PreOperational first" ; default : return canopen_client :: ToString ( e ); } } Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: the core, the port contract, and your port. The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into CAN frames (SDO requests, NMT commands, SYNC, PDOs) and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port puts each frame on the bus and hands received frames back. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/canopen_client.hpp public calls ; inc/canopen_client_can_interface.hpp CanInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layer Files Owns Core inc/canopen_client.hpp , src/canopen_client.ipp Client<Port> : lifecycle, the one request in flight, SDO transfers, the receive router, node table, EMCY queue, PDO configuration, the drive state machine Protocol inc/canopen_client_protocol.hpp Pure constexpr frame builders and parsers: NMT, SDO, heartbeat, EMCY, SYNC, PDO, statusword decode; no state, no port Types inc/canopen_client_types.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config , presets, identifiers, capacities Port contract inc/canopen_client_can_interface.hpp The CRTP base, the CanPort and CanRxPort concepts Platform port Your class The CAN controller: EnsureInitialized , Send , Receive , NowUs , optionally Log Two port levels ¶ A port with EnsureInitialized() and Send() satisfies CanPort : the client can command ( SendNmt , SendSync , SendRpdo , SdoDownloadUnconfirmed ). Adding Receive() and NowUs() satisfies CanRxPort and enables everything that needs a reply: SDO, heartbeat, guarding, EMCY, TPDO, PDO configuration and the drive helpers. A call that needs a reply on a send-only port does not compile; a port that has only one of Receive and NowUs is refused by a static_assert . One request in flight ¶ The client runs one SDO transfer at a time and every call blocks until it ends. While it waits for a reply, other frames that arrive are not lost: heartbeats update the node table, EMCY frames are queued and TPDOs are stored, and a flood of unrelated frames cannot hold a request past its timeout ( Stats::flood_aborts ). The driver starts no thread, sleeps only through the port's Receive() and takes no lock. Fixed capacities ¶ Resource Capacity Full means Monitored nodes 16 ( kMonitorCapacity ) MonitorNode() returns BufferTooSmall Subscribed TPDOs 16 ( kPdoSubscriptionCapacity ) SubscribeTpdo() returns BufferTooSmall Queued EMCY events 8 ( kEmcyQueueCapacity ) The oldest are kept; new ones are dropped and counted in Stats::emcy_dropped Entries in a PDO mapping 16 ( kMaxPdoEntries ) ValidatePdoConfig() refuses it Next: Contract .

While it waits for a reply, other frames that arrive are not lost: heartbeats update the node table, EMCY frames are queued and TPDOs are stored, and a flood of unrelated frames cannot hold a request past its timeout ( Stats::flood_aborts ). The driver starts no thread, sleeps only through the port's Receive() and takes no lock.

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the CANopen client promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() validates the configuration ( InvalidArgument before the port is touched), starts the port and clears the node table, the PDO subscriptions, the EMCY queue and the counters. Afterwards it returns Ok with no I/O. Every call that sends or receives returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and that wins over InvalidArgument . No call starts the port as a side effect. InvalidArgument means nothing was sent and nothing was read. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; a missing or silent node is Timeout ; a node that refuses a transfer is SdoAbort with the node's code in GetLastAbort() . One request is in flight at a time and every call blocks until it ends or its timeout expires. After a timeout the driver sends an SDO abort ( Config::abort_on_timeout ) so the node's server is released. A reply is accepted only when its identifier is the node's, its command specifier fits the request and, for a segmented transfer, its toggle bit alternates. A lying node cannot overrun the caller's buffer, finish a transfer it has not completed, or keep a call running past its timeout. A segmented upload that does not fit the caller's buffer is aborted with 0x05040005 and returns BufferTooSmall ; nothing is written past the buffer. A PDO configuration that fails part-way leaves the PDO invalid, never half configured and valid. DriveDisable() and DriveQuickStop() are never refused for the drive's state: they are sent up to Config::safety_attempts times. When Receive() fails the driver drops its receive state, sends the frame anyway and reports Bus afterwards. SendNmt(Stop) is a single attempt (NMT has no confirmation) and also sends past a failing receive side. A wait ends when its time budget is spent, counted only on frames the port returns; Timeout returns do not consume the frame budget. A drive wait is bounded by Config::drive_timeout_us , however small the poll period. DriveResetFault() spends one drive_timeout_us in all (the fault-reaction wait and the wait for the fault to clear share one clock). Under a flood of frames a pause between two polls ends after kMaxFramesPerWait frames, so the iteration is shorter than the poll interval and the step limit ( drive_timeout_us / drive_poll_interval_us + 2 ) can end the wait before the timeout: always early (a Timeout ), never late. DriveResetFault() writes 0x0000 (Disable voltage, the state the drive is in) after the fault has cleared, so controlword bit 7 is not left high. Node ages ( alive , the Stopped gate) are compared in 32 bits of NowUs() , which wraps at 71.6 minutes: a heartbeat older than that can look fresh. Call GetNodeStatus() or Poll() at least once an hour, or treat a node with no recent count change as lost. The waits (SDO, guard, drive) are wrap-safe. Frames that arrive while a drive wait pauses between polls are routed (heartbeats, EMCY, TPDOs), not lost. ReadRawSdo() , WriteRawSdo() , SendRawFrame() and ReadRawFrame() are single-shot diagnostic access: no retry, no validation beyond framing. The raw frame returned is a copy owned by the driver ( GetLastRawFrame() ). They bypass the safety and state guards : no node-state gate, and any frame can go out, including an NMT command, an RPDO or a drive controlword. They do not update the node table (a raw NMT Stop leaves the table saying Operational), so stop and disable must use SendNmt() , DriveDisable() and DriveQuickStop() . ReadRawSdo() and WriteRawSdo() drain the receive queue first (frames are routed as usual), so the frame they return is the first one that arrives after their request; ReadRawFrame() returns whatever is next, including an older frame. The Send hook gets a frame the driver owns, valid only during the call: copy it to queue it. (The driver keeps it in a member that the next send overwrites.) A node whose heartbeat says it is Stopped is refused SDO calls with NodeState and no frame is sent. Ambiguities and how the driver reads them ¶ Exact-size reads. The typed reads ( SdoReadU8() , SdoReadU16() , SdoReadU32() ) require the node's reply to be exactly the size asked for; any other size is Protocol and the value is not used. Stale replies. CANopen has no request identifier: a late reply to a request that timed out can be taken for the reply to the next request on the same node and index. The driver checks the identifier, the command specifier, the toggle bit and (for typed reads) the size, but cannot rule this out; abort_on_timeout keeps the window short. Boot-up. A node's boot-up message sets bootup_seen for that node. It stays set until ClearBootUp(node) or EnsureInitialized() , so an application can tell a restart from a long silence. Bus-off. After a bus-off the port recovers the controller; the application then calls Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() so the node table and the receive state start clean. Guarding. A guard reply whose toggle bit repeats returns Protocol , and the driver resynchronises to the toggle it saw, so the next reply is judged against the node's. A boot-up message (state 0) that arrives while a guard request is out is recorded ( bootup_seen ) and is not taken for the reply; the wait goes on. What is not verified ¶ Hardware. The driver has been run only against a model of the bus and its nodes. Treat every timing as not verified on hardware until the bench steps on the Troubleshooting page have been run on a real node. The specifications. CiA 301 and CiA 402 are published behind a registration or a purchase and were not obtained. The byte layouts, the order of operations and the statusword masks come from public sources named in docs/datasheets.yml (an encyclopaedia article, a vendor tutorial, the open-source CANopenNode and python-canopen projects). Where a public source and the specification could differ, the driver does the stricter thing, and a node that does something unusual may be refused. Block transfer, CAN FD, extended identifiers, LSS, NMT slave and SDO server are not implemented. An extended-identifier, CAN FD or error frame must be dropped by the port before Receive() returns. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates canopen_client_version.h Your port A CAN controller: send, receive with a timeout, a microsecond clock Threading ¶ Not thread-safe; takes no lock. One owner task, or one mutex around every call. Nothing may run in an ISR: a call waits inside the port's Receive() . Errors ¶ Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Before EnsureInitialized() succeeded, or after Deinitialize() InvalidArgument 2 An argument or a Config field is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 The port failed to send or to receive Timeout 4 No valid reply in time: SDO, node guarding or a drive state change DeviceFault 8 A read-back ( Verify::ReadBack ) showed a value other than the one written Unsupported 9 ReadPdoConfig() met a 29-bit PDO identifier SdoAbort 16 The node aborted the SDO transfer; the code is in GetLastAbort() Protocol 17 A reply broke the protocol: command specifier, toggle bit or size BufferTooSmall 18 An upload is larger than the caller's buffer, or a fixed table is full InvalidFrame 19 A frame fails validation; returned by the codecs, counted by the client NodeState 20 The node's NMT state ignores the request DriveFault 21 The drive is in Fault, or in a state no transition leaves DeviceIdMismatch , Crc and Busy are never returned: the CAN controller checks the frame CRC, and calls block. Memory ¶ No heap, exceptions, RTTI or static mutable state. The object holds a port reference, a Config , the node table (16), the TPDO subscriptions (16), the EMCY queue (8) and one transfer state; its size is fixed at compile time. Platform ¶ Platform-free; the ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated bus and drive node, through the host port host_canopen_client_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/canopen_client_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest canopen_client_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ An ESP-IDF application that runs the driver on an ESP32-C6 with the TWAI controller and a CAN transceiver; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_canopen_client_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What a CAN node needs: a controller, a transceiver, a terminated bus. The driver sees only the port's Send() and Receive() ; this page shows the reference wiring with the TI SN65HVD230 3.3 V transceiver, the one part whose datasheet was obtained for this repository. Datasheet sections this page relies on Pin configuration: Texas Instruments SN65HVD230, SN65HVD231, SN65HVD232 (SLOS346) O, 7 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 5 Supply voltage and mode select (RS): Texas Instruments SN65HVD230, SN65HVD231, SN65HVD232 (SLOS346) O, 8.3 Recommended Operating Conditions; 5 Description (continued), p. 6 CAN node: transceiver and controller wiring: Texas Instruments SN65HVD230, SN65HVD231, SN65HVD232 (SLOS346) O, 11.2 Typical Application, p. 26 Bus termination: Texas Instruments SN65HVD230, SN65HVD231, SN65HVD232 (SLOS346) O, 11.2.1.1 CAN Termination, p. 26 Pre-defined connection set (COB-IDs): Wikipedia contributors Wikipedia article (oldid 1373604442) last edited September 2026, Pre-defined connection set, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The CANopen specifications themselves (CiA 301 and CiA 402) were not obtained; see Contract . The driver does not depend on the transceiver: any ISO 11898-2 part with the same four signals works. Pins ¶ SOIC-8, 8 pins (7 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 5 ). Pin Name Type (domain) Function Driver hook If unused Datasheet 1 D digital in (VCC) CAN transmit data (TXD): low is dominant, high is recessive Send(const CanFrame&) - 7, p. 5 2 GND ground Ground - - 7, p. 5 3 VCC power (VCC) Transceiver 3.3 V supply - - 8.3, p. 6 4 R digital out (VCC) CAN receive data (RXD): low is dominant, high is recessive Receive(CanFrame&, timeout_us) - 7, p. 5 5 Vref analog (VCC) VCC / 2 reference output - Leave open 10.3.1, p. 20 6 CANL bus (VCC) Low-level CAN bus line - - 7, p. 5 7 CANH bus (VCC) High-level CAN bus line - - 7, p. 5 8 RS digital in (VCC) Mode select: pull-down to GND is high speed, pull-up to VCC is low power, 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ is slope control - Tie to GND for high speed 10.4, p. 20 Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . The driver reaches the bus through two hooks. Send() hands a frame to the controller, which drives D. Receive() waits for a frame the controller took from R. Pin levels, bit timing, arbitration and the frame CRC stay in the controller. Supply and mode ¶ Parameter Value Where Supply, VCC 3.0 V to 3.6 V Recommended operating conditions RS to GND High-speed mode Device functional modes RS to VCC Low-power standby Device functional modes RS through 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ to GND Slope control (slower edges) Device functional modes The port should leave RS at the level that gives the mode you want before the first Send() ; a transceiver in standby does not drive the bus, and the driver cannot tell that from a missing node ( Timeout ). Bus termination ¶ The bus is a twisted pair of about 120 Ω, terminated with 120 Ω at each of its two ends and nowhere else. A bus with no or one terminator can work at short range and then fail in ways that look like random Timeout results ( Troubleshooting ). 60 Ω between CANH and CANL on a powered-off bus shows both terminators. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( canopen_client_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-canopen-client.git external/driver-canopen-client git submodule update --init external/driver-canopen-client Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-canopen-client ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE canopen_client::canopen_client ) canopen_client::canopen_client is an alias of the canopen_client INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect CANOPEN_CLIENT_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver CANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-canopen-client -B build-canopen_client cmake --install build-canopen_client --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( canopen_client 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE canopen_client::canopen_client ) The target is canopen_client::canopen_client in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated canopen_client_version.h go to include/canopen_client/inc/ , the template implementation to include/canopen_client/src/canopen_client.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-canopen-client) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-canopen-client (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-canopen-client.git components/canopen_client canopen_client (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml canopen_client (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : canopen_client : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-canopen-client.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES canopen_client (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. It has no false-positive tolerance : before merging, it runs over every finished driver and the template; any finding on a driver that CI shows clean is a false positive, and the lint is not merged until it has none (narrow the pattern; do not add an ignore list per driver). It may be conservative the other way (miss cases): then the catalogue says partial and names the review question that covers the rest. It never edits files, never skips silently (a missing tool is reported as a skipped step in the final line, and the gate treats a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step as a failure), and has a selftest with one bad and one good case. It does not replace the CI scan: CI is the final word for MISRA. Recording a new finding ¶ Append the finding to its catalogue entry (driver, review round or CI report file, finding id) and update the count and the index table; add a new entry only when no class fits. Write the check at the level the rules above give: the lint, or the test pattern (model knob, mutant, fuzz property), or the reviewer's question in the skill. Run it over the finished drivers (lint) or add the regression test that fails without the fix (test). Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] and the template change is released as a new template commit; drivers take it with scaffold.py --check-drift --fix (the skills and tools are managed files), which updates the template pin in .kokeb/template.yml . Mention the catalogue id in the commit subject. The pre-push gate ¶ A driver is cleared for its first push only by kokeb-tools/gate.sh <chip> (the orchestrator's script, one run per driver through the shared Docker lock). It writes a log and a verdict, and PASS needs all of: container preflight ( tools/preflight.sh --container ) with 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) , including the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds; a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step is a FAIL; handbook_check reports 0 errors (this includes the library-subset include scan); tools/check_standalone.py passes; template drift: scaffold.py --check-drift reports nothing; no .pdf file is tracked; the examples/esp32/scripts gitlink (mode 160000) is present; the tree is staged as it will be committed. No silent skips: every step prints a line, and a missing tool fails the gate. Roles ¶ Builders write code, models, tests and docs and run host tests and the quick preflight. They do not run the container gate, push, or create repositories. The gate runner is one serialized worker that runs gate.sh for one driver at a time and reports the verdict and the log; it does not edit the driver. Reviewers are read-only and independent. They are given the code, the model, the datasheet, the catalogue and the previous round's report, and never the builder's conclusions (the build report is read only in the claims-vs-code step). They run the review-round protocol. Fixers change the driver, fix at the cause, add the test that fails without the fix, and answer each finding id. The template maintainer applies promotions and keeps the catalogue current. Backlog of promotions (state of the catalogue) ¶ The classes whose target level is above their present level are listed in the catalogue index: RD-12 to RD-18 and RD-23 (MISRA patterns, one misra_lint with a rule per id), RD-20 and RD-22 (ESP-IDF and compile-fail lints), RD-08 ( claims-symbols ), RD-07 (model standalone lint), RD-06, RD-01, RD-02, RD-03, RD-05, RD-10 and RD-25 (shared model knobs and a template mutation runner), RD-21 (host start-up test of the ESP32 port).

Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SN65HVD230, SN65HVD231, SN65HVD232 (SLOS346) O: Supply voltage and mode select (RS): 8.3 Recommended Operating Conditions; 5 Description (continued), p. 6 CAN node: transceiver and controller wiring: 11.2 Typical Application, p. 26 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. Guards no test kills (surviving mutants) 6 review test RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules 3 review test RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI 4 CI lint RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing 6 review review RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit 3 review review RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard 3 test test RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read 2 review test RD-32 Docs style: line length, merged bullets, stale text 3 lint lint RD-33 Another project's name or dated history 1 lint lint Chip-protocol and safety classes ¶ RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.

docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).
docs.title: RD-11 Header outside the library subset

docs.text: Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != .
docs.title: RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic

docs.text: Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests .
docs.title: RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses

docs.text: Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned).
docs.title: RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended.
docs.title: RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp .
docs.title: RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ

docs.text: Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?"
docs.title: RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type

docs.text: Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision.
docs.title: RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2

docs.text: Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call.
docs.title: RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete

docs.text: Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?"
docs.title: RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults

docs.text: Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert .
docs.title: RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler

docs.text: Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.
