docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the pins, a fuzzer that controls what the driver reads, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_protocol.cpp The frame codecs: NMT, SDO, heartbeat, EMCY, SYNC, PDO, statusword, and their rejects tests/test_sdo.cpp Expedited and segmented transfers, abort codes, replies that lie, timeouts tests/test_rx.cpp NMT, heartbeat, guarding, EMCY, SYNC and TPDO on the receive path tests/test_pdo.cpp PDO configuration in the profile's order, failure leaves the PDO invalid tests/test_drive.cpp The CiA 402 state machine, safety retries, remapped objects tests/test_lifecycle.cpp NotInitialized , InvalidArgument sends nothing, the send-only port, every Error returned tests/test_faults.cpp A send or receive failure injected at every step of every call tests/test_boundaries.cpp Both sides of every numeric limit tests/test_hardening.cpp The review fixes: raw access, switch-off with a failing receive side, time-bound drive waits, toggle and size checks, node range limits, PDO bounds tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( canopen_client_fuzz_canopen_client_corpus ), see below tests/mock_canopen_client.hpp The bus, the node and drive models and the mock ports, written from the protocol and not from the driver's codecs tests/compile_fail/ Ports and calls that must not compile tests/check_install.cmake find_package(canopen_client) from an installed package The tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads is what arrives on the bus, so the frames, their timing and the port's failures are what a hostile or broken node controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_canopen_client.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration, then up to 400 driver calls, and for each frame the port sends or receives whether it fails, times out, is injected or is answered by the node model. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error this driver returns (never Crc , Busy or DeviceIdMismatch ) and T{} ; before EnsureInitialized() every call returns NotInitialized , and InvalidArgument means no frame was sent; an upload never reports more bytes than the caller's buffer holds, and the EMCY queue never holds more than its capacity; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message; DriveDisable() , DriveQuickStop() and SendNmt(Stop) attempt a send once started, even when the port's receive side fails. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_canopen_client ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_canopen_client -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_canopen_client The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_canopen_client , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_canopen_client/ on GCC and Clang ( canopen_client_fuzz_canopen_client_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( canopen_client_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/canopen_client.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml with the repository root as the driver's component. The gate needs it too.

To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DCANOPEN_CLIENT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( canopen_client_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/canopen_client.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

docs.text: Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml with the repository root as the driver's component. The gate needs it too.

Symptom Likely cause Fix EnsureInitialized() returns Bus The port could not start the controller Check the pins, the bit rate and that no other code owns the peripheral EnsureInitialized() returns InvalidArgument A Config field is out of range Check it with canopen_client::Validate() ( Configuration ) Every SDO call returns Timeout Wrong bit rate or node id, no termination, transceiver in standby, node not powered Check the bit rate on every node, 60 Ω between CANH and CANL ( Hardware ), RS at ground Some calls time out, others work A receive filter drops an identifier, or a node is slow Accept 0x080 to 0x7FF; use SlowBusPreset() SdoAbort The node refused the object GetLastAbort() : 0x06020000 object missing, 0x06010002 write to a read-only object, 0x06090011 sub-index missing NodeState with no frame sent The node's heartbeat says it is Stopped SendNmt(Start, node) or SendNmt(PreOperational, node) Protocol The node's reply broke the rules, or a short SDO frame with strict length Try strict_sdo_length = false if the node sends short frames BufferTooSmall from an upload The object is larger than your buffer Pass a bigger buffer; the transfer was aborted with 0x05040005 DriveEnable() returns Timeout The drive did not reach Operation enabled in drive_timeout_us Raise it (the wait is bounded by this time, not by a step count); read ReadStatusword() for the state the drive stopped in DriveEnable() returns DriveFault The drive is in Fault Fix the cause, then DriveResetFault() A node is never alive Its heartbeat producer time is 0, or it is not registered WriteHeartbeatProducerTime() , then MonitorNode() with a timeout above the period Stats::emcy_dropped grows The EMCY queue (8) is not drained Call PopEmcy() after every Poll() Bench steps ¶ None of the driver's timing has run on hardware. To confirm it on a node: read 0x1000 with ReadDeviceType() and compare it with the node's documentation; start the node and watch GetNodeStatus() follow its heartbeat; write a read-only object and check SdoAbort with 0x06010002 comes back; unplug the node and check Timeout within sdo_timeout_us . Record the result in the pull request.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Inside the SN65HVD230 ¶ Inside the SN65HVD230 Figure description and sources The SN65HVD230's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml SN65HVD230: A CAN node ¶ SN65HVD230: A CAN node Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml SN65HVD230 package, SOIC-8 ¶ SN65HVD230 package, SOIC-8 Figure description and sources The SN65HVD230 package seen from the top and, when the height is known, from the side, drawn to scale: 4.9 x 3.9 x 1.75 mm. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side at the stated pitch; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml SN65HVD230 pinout, SOIC-8 ¶ SN65HVD230 pinout, SOIC-8 Figure description and sources The SN65HVD230 seen from the top, in its SOIC-8 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml The layers, one of them yours ¶ The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into CAN frames (SDO requests, NMT commands, SYNC, PDOs) and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port puts each frame on the bus and hands received frames back. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.
